header_verdict: All four drains take the sub-vector header itself in rdi -- in the drops, the lea of record +0x18 (#2714).  The header is 24 bytes: the word at +0x0 is the capacity word (the drops size their post-drain buffer free by it, word * 0x10, and the unwind drains free by it the same way); the word at +0x8 is the buffer pointer; the word at +0x10 is the live element count.  The normal drains load exactly the +0x8 and +0x10 header words (header census), so the record word at +0x28 that #2714 found never loaded by the drop bodies is the sub-vector length, and it is loaded here -- as header +0x10.  The buffer holds 0x10-byte elements.
element_verdict: Per element, the normal drains (0x153deb0 / 0x474e8a0) walk the buffer in order with a cursor seeded at buffer + 0x18 (loads at cursor -0x18 / -0x10, advancing 0x10 per element, counted by the header +0x10 word).  Each element is a tagged pair {data at +0x0, descriptor at +0x8} -- the same element shape #2559 staged and the drops consume at record level.  For each pair: descriptor word 0 is called on the data when non-null (0x153deff / 0x474e8ef); then descriptor word +0x8 is loaded as the size and, when non-zero, the data is freed through the dealloc target loaded once from slot 0x64df4a0 (RELATIVE target 0x635de30, called through r13) with the size class computed from descriptor words +0x8 (size) and +0x10 (align) by the tzcnt/cmov idiom (tzcnt at 0x153df0e / 0x474e8fe; class 0 when align <= size, the tzcnt otherwise, and the tzcnt whenever align >= 0x11) -- the same descriptor protocol as the drops' tagged pair, one level down.  The normal drain does NOT free the buffer: on the drops' normal path the caller frees it afterwards by the capacity word (#2714 stage 2).  A zero length returns immediately.
unwind_verdict: The 86-byte bodies (0x1539990 / 0x474e270) are drain-and-free wrappers, not a second drain implementation: each calls its own module's normal drain on the header (0x1539997 / 0x474e277), then frees the buffer itself -- capacity word at header +0x0 loaded (0x153999c / 0x474e27c), buffer pointer at +0x8, size word << 4, align 0 -- as a tail jump through the dealloc slot 0x64df4a0, gated on the capacity word.  This is exactly the free the drops perform inline on their normal path, which is why the drops' first landing pads route here: on the unwind path the inline free never runs.  Each wrapper's own landing pad saves the exception, re-runs the same buffer free through the slot (0x15399d8 / 0x474e2b8), and resumes through _Unwind_Resume (PLT 0x63f0a50).  Inside the normal drains, the landing pad (0x153df39 / 0x474e929) saves the exception, re-runs the interrupted element's descriptor free through the dealloc slot with the pad cmov variant (class 0 unless align > size), hands each remaining element pairwise -- data word, descriptor word, cursor advancing 0x10 -- to the pair-destroy helper (0x1537b00 / 0x474e0b0, 130 bytes each, hash-pinned boundaries here), and resumes through _Unwind_Resume; the normal-drain FDE's final instruction is a call through the cleanup slot 0x64df4c0 (RELATIVE target 0x1680cab) at 0x153df95 / 0x474e985, whose continuation lies outside the FDE.
clone_verdict: Both same-size pairs are clones at the pinned instruction shape, judged by the #2714 method (unmasked instruction diff + consumption order).  The 235-byte normal drains decode to identical instruction offsets (72 instructions each) and, after masking the address-dependent tails of branch and slot instructions, byte-identical streams; the unmasked difference is exactly five sites -- three RIP-relative displacements (the dealloc slot load, the pad dealloc call, and the cleanup-slot tail call, all to the same slots in both instances) and two rel32 calls (the module-local pair-destroy helper and the shared _Unwind_Resume PLT entry).  The 86-byte unwind drains are identical under the same test (29 instructions each, exactly four differing sites): two RIP-relative dealloc-slot references to the same slot and two rel32 calls (the module-local normal-drain target and the shared _Unwind_Resume).  Consumption order is the same in both pairs: the vec-A and reader instances read the same header words, walk the same cursor, and free through the same slots.  The bodies' own hashes differ, as the pinned records show; identity is claimed at the masked instruction shape only.
census_verdict: Direct-call census over the whole .text (sites attributed by containing FDE): the drains are shared helpers, not drop-private.  Each normal drain has exactly nine direct call sites and each unwind drain exactly two, with matching counts per module.  The vec-A normal drain 0x153deb0 is called by the element drop 0x1538ec0 (0x1538f28), by its unwind wrapper (0x1539997), from FDE 0x1538460 (0x1538559) and from six further FDEs (0x1569cd0, 0x156a010, 0x158b8e0, 0x15ac910, 0x15bb960, 0x15bf200); the vec-A unwind drain 0x1539990 only from the element drop's first landing pad (0x1538f92) and from FDE 0x1538460 (0x15386a3).  The reader normal drain 0x474e8a0 is called by the reader element drop (0x474dd38), by its unwind wrapper (0x474e277), by the merge delegate 0x4748500 (0x47487ed -- the call the merge-delegate packet #2615 recorded while leaving this body a hash-pinned boundary), and from six further FDEs (0x4747cb0, 0x4747f50, 0x474dba0, 0x47530e0, 0x47531d0, 0x4753450); the reader unwind drain 0x474e270 only from the reader drop's first landing pad (0x474dda2) and from FDE 0x474dba0 (0x474dc56).  All non-drop callers are recorded by FDE range only; several are 86-byte FDEs whose shape matches the unwind wrappers, not traced here.  No other direct caller of any of the four exists in the binary.
limits: Static trace only.  Hash-pinned, not traced: the two element drops (#2714 owners, retained here as boundary context), the two pair-destroy helpers 0x1537b00 / 0x474e0b0 the normal drains' landing pads hand remaining elements to, the dealloc target 0x635de30, the cleanup target 0x1680cab, and _Unwind_Resume.  Non-drop callers of the drains are recorded by FDE range only, and whether every caller passes the same 24-byte header layout is established only for the drops' sites (record +0x18) and the merge delegate's element +0x18/+0x20 site recorded by #2615.  What the elements' descriptor drop functions do beyond the call, and any semantic name for the element type, are not claimed.  No captured code executed, no runtime value or reconstruction gate is claimed.
